title: Scholarship and Locker
premise: Theo Eastwick just wants to survive senior year unnoticed at Hollowmere Academy, a school built atop the sealed foundations of the town's original settlement. But his late grandmother's recipe box holds not recipes but instructions — for unlocking the 'locker' beneath the school, where the town's founders bound something that fed on ambition. The annual Founders' Championship, a seemingly trivial academic-and-athletics contest, is actually the ritual that keeps the seal renewed; this year, headmaster Dr. Vane has been quietly feeding students' loyalty and secrets to the thing below to extend his own power. Theo must win both championships — the public one and the hidden one of wills beneath it — while deciding whether to expose the truth that would shatter the found family he's finally built. He wins by refusing to win alone: he breaks the seal by sharing the binding freely among everyone, ending Vane's power and freeing the school at the cost of the scholarship that was supposed to be his escape.
about_author: Zephyrine Villalobos is a former boarding-school cook who swears half her recipes came from a box she never wrote. She lives in a coastal town with too many cellars and writes stories about kids who find family in unlikely places.

chapters.title: The New Kid Math
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Arriving mid-year at Hollowmere on partial scholarship, Theo maps the social terrain and resolves to stay invisible. A stray comment from janitor Mr. Okafor about 'the old floor plan' under the gym plants unease. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness masking hope.

chapters.title: Grandma's Box
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Sorting his grandmother's belongings in the dorm attic, Theo finds her recipe box — index cards with measurements that are clearly coordinates, timings, and warnings. One card names Hollowmere. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into curiosity; first crack in his invisibility plan.

chapters.title: The Misfit Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Priya, debate-team captain and cafeteria outcast. Priya recruits Theo for the Championship team of misfits; he resists, then joins when he realizes team access means access to restricted archives. Emotional beat: reluctant belonging beginning.

chapters.title: What Vane Knows
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Researching the school's founding, Theo discovers every championship roster since 1911 lists students who later vanished from records. Dr. Vane catches him in the archive — and is oddly kind. Emotional beat: dread dressed as flattery; Theo senses being watched.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Currency
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Vane offers Priya a full ride if she reports on her teammates. She almost takes it; instead she warns Theo, cementing their trust. Meanwhile teammate Marcus's behavior turns strangely compliant after a private meeting with Vane. Emotional beat: loyalty tested and chosen.

chapters.title: Below the Gymnasium
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Following grandma's cards, Theo and Priya breach the sealed sub-basement and find the locker: an iron door humming with borrowed voices, including, faintly, his grandmother's. They learn the Championship is the renewal rite. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Price of Winning
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus, drained and hollowed, confesses what Vane took from him — his memory of why he loved running. The team realizes winning the public Championship feeds the thing below. Theo must throw the contest or lose his friends. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as victimhood; resolve hardens.

chapters.title: Cards on the Table
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo reveals his grandmother helped build the original binding — and betrayed the town by hiding the escape clause in a recipe box. Vane corners him with an offer: win, and get the full scholarship plus his grandmother's voice back. Emotional beat: temptation aimed straight at his grief.

chapters.title: The Championship That Matters
chapters.summary: Full-team POV rotation during the Championship day. Instead of competing individually, the team performs the binding together, each speaking a piece of the recipe aloud — sharing the burden so no one person holds the power. Vane tries to force-feed the seal; the voices below turn on him. Emotional beat: climax of collective courage over individual glory.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine (Actually)
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue weeks later. The school stands, ordinary and strange; Vane is gone, the sub-basement a storage room again. Theo lost the scholarship but gained a family who refuses to let him leave alone — Priya's mom offers him a room, Okafor winks. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
